revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Overtime Hours Limit
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen's team can use at most 40 hours of overtime this week to close the case. So far the team has logged 26 hours. Write an inequality for the additional overtime hours t the team can still use, solve it, and graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The inequality is 26 + t ≤ 40. Subtracting 26 from both sides: t ≤ 40 − 26 = 14. Since ≤ includes the boundary, graph a closed circle at 14 and shade left (toward smaller values), meaning the team can use 14 or fewer additional overtime hours this week.

vocabulary.definition: Represent a range of possible values with <, >, ≤, or ≥.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Representar un rango de valores posibles con <, >, ≤ o ≥.
vocabulary.visual: You must be at least 12 years old: a ≥ 12.
vocabulary.cloze: Use <, >, ≤ or ≥ when the answer is a ___ of values rather than one.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence that compares two sides with <, >, ≤, or ≥.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática que compara dos lados con <, >, ≤ o ≥.
vocabulary.visual: x > 5 means x can be 6, 7, 8, ... — any number greater than 5
vocabulary.cloze: A math sentence comparing values with <, >, ≤, or ≥ is an ___.

examples.why: It compares values with a greater-than sign.
That is an equation, not an inequality.

vocabulary.definition: The > sign, showing one number is bigger.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El signo >, que muestra que un número es mayor.
vocabulary.cloze: The symbol > that means one value is larger than another means ___.

vocabulary.definition: The < sign, showing one number is smaller.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El signo <, que muestra que un número es menor.
vocabulary.cloze: The symbol < that means one value is smaller than another means ___.

vocabulary.visual: 'At least 10 players' → p ≥ 10 (could be 10, 11, 12, ...); 'At most 5 tries' → t ≤ 5 (could be 5, 4, 3, ...)
vocabulary.cloze: 'At least' means greater than or equal to, and 'at most' means ___ than or equal to.

vocabulary.definition: A letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can change.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una letra que representa un número desconocido o que puede cambiar.
vocabulary.visual: In x > 5, the letter x stands for any number greater than 5.
vocabulary.cloze: A letter that stands for an unknown number is a ___.

examples.why: A letter for the unknown amount.

vocabulary.definition: A phrase meaning less than or equal to (≤).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una frase que significa menor o igual que (≤).
vocabulary.cloze: The phrase that means less than or equal to is "no more than," written with the ___ symbol.

vocabulary.termEs: Representar desigualdades en una recta numérica
vocabulary.definition: Show every solution to an inequality on a number line with a boundary point and an arrow.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mostrar cada solución de una desigualdad en una recta numérica con un punto límite y una flecha.
vocabulary.visual: x > 3 uses an open circle at 3 and an arrow to the right.
vocabulary.cloze: Mark the ___ ___, then shade every value that makes it true.

examples.text: Open circle at 6, shaded right, for x > 6
examples.why: Circle style and direction both match.

vocabulary.definition: Isolate the variable, then show the complete solution set on a number line.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Aislar la variable y luego mostrar el conjunto completo de soluciones en una recta numérica.
vocabulary.visual: x + 2 ≤ 7 → x ≤ 5; closed circle at 5, arrow left.
vocabulary.cloze: Isolate the variable first, then show the whole ___ ___ on a number line.

vocabulary.termEs: Resolución de problemas con ecuaciones y desigualdades
vocabulary.definition: Use an equation for one exact value or an inequality for a range of values in a real situation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar una ecuación para un valor exacto o una desigualdad para un rango de valores en una situación real.
vocabulary.cloze: Use an equation for one exact value and an ___ for a range.

vocabulary.definition: A straight line where numbers are placed in order; numbers get smaller to the left and larger to the right.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una recta donde los números se colocan en orden; los números son menores a la izquierda y mayores a la derecha.
vocabulary.visual: A horizontal line with marks at 0, 1, 2, 3, ... showing where values fall
vocabulary.cloze: A line with numbers in order used to show values and solutions is a ___.

examples.text: A line with 6 marked and values increasing right
A list of the same numbers
examples.why: No positions, so nothing to shade.

vocabulary.definition: To find the number that makes it true.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Encontrar el número que la hace verdadera.
vocabulary.visual: x + 3 > 10 → subtract 3 → x > 7 — any number greater than 7 works
vocabulary.cloze: To find all the values that make an inequality true is to ___ it.

examples.why: The value that makes it true.

vocabulary.definition: To show a real-life situation with an equation or inequality.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mostrar una situación real con una ecuación o desigualdad.
vocabulary.visual: 'Twice a number is 18' → 2n = 18 — the equation models the words
vocabulary.cloze: A drawing, equation, or diagram that represents a situation is a ___.

examples.text: Writing 12n = 500 for the car wash goal
examples.why: The situation as a number sentence.

vocabulary.definition: An empty circle showing a number is NOT included.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un círculo vacío que muestra que un número NO está incluido.
vocabulary.visual: x > 5: open circle at 5 means 5 itself is NOT a solution, but 5.1, 6, 7, ... are
vocabulary.cloze: A hollow circle that shows a value is NOT included, used for < or >, is an ___.

examples.why: 3 is not included when the symbol is >.
≥ includes 3, so it needs a closed circle.

vocabulary.definition: To show answers on a number line with circles and shading.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mostrar respuestas en una recta numérica con círculos y sombreado.
vocabulary.visual: x > 7: open circle at 7, shade right — shows all solutions at a glance
vocabulary.cloze: To show the solutions on a number line is to ___ them.

examples.text: An open circle at 8 with shading to the right
examples.why: Circle and shading show the solutions.

examples.text: A dot at 8 with no shading
examples.why: It shows one value, not the set.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign showing both sides are the same.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con un signo igual que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: A math sentence with an equal sign is an ___.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 8.4–8.7: 8.4 Write and Represent Inequalities, 8.5 Understand Inequalities and Their Solutions, 8.6 Solve and Graph Inequalities, 8.7 Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 8.4–8.7
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 8.4: 'At least' means ≥ and 'at most' means ≤; 'more than' means > and 'fewer/less than' means <. • 8.5: Closed circle for ≤ or ≥ (included), open circle for < or > (not included); shade right for greater, left for less. • 8.6: Solve with inverse operations, then graph the solution set: open circle for < or >, closed for ≤ or ≥. • 8.7: 'Equals' or 'exactly' points to an equation (=); 'at least, at most, more than, fewer than' points to an inequality.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 8.4 — Write and Represent Inequalities: 'At least' means ≥ and 'at most' means ≤; 'more than' means > and 'fewer/less than' means <.
Lesson 8.5 — Understand Inequalities and Their Solutions: Closed circle for ≤ or ≥ (included), open circle for < or > (not included); shade right for greater, left for less.
Lesson 8.6 — Solve and Graph Inequalities: Solve with inverse operations, then graph the solution set: open circle for < or >, closed for ≤ or ≥.
Lesson 8.7 — Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving: 'Equals' or 'exactly' points to an equation (=); 'at least, at most, more than, fewer than' points to an inequality.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson

From 8.5: Graph x < 5. What number is the boundary?
From 8.6: Solve x − 5 ≤ 8. What is the inverse of subtracting 5?
From 8.7: Clue: 'The lookout earned less than $50.' Equation or inequality?

youDo.title: Show you're caught up
lines: The practice below mixes problems from Lessons 8.4–8.7. Each problem is tagged with its lesson number.
Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.instructions: Read each word problem. Decide if it needs an equation or an inequality. Write the mathematical model, solve it, and check your answer for reasonableness.

rows.wordProblem: A detective splits 42 clues equally among 6 case boards. How many clues per board?
rows.reasonable: Yes — 7 clues per board makes sense.

rows.wordProblem: A witness says the suspect carried fewer than 10 items. If the suspect already had 3, how many more could they carry?
rows.reasonable: Yes — up to 6 more items is reasonable.

rows.wordProblem: The evidence room needs at least 50 storage bins. They already have 28. How many more do they need?
rows.reasonable: Yes — at least 22 more bins makes sense.

hints: If the problem uses 'is,' 'equals,' or 'gives exactly,' use an equation (=). If it uses 'at least,' 'at most,' 'more than,' or 'fewer than,' use an inequality.
After solving, ask: Does my answer make sense in the real-world context? Could the number be negative? A fraction of a person?
explore.label: For each word problem, write the model, solve, and check for reasonableness.

discourse.prompt: How do you decide whether a word problem needs an equation or an inequality?
discourse.sentenceFrame: I use an equation when the problem says ___, but I use an inequality when the problem says ___ because ___.

diagram.intro: Now write the solving steps on paper-style lines — I'll check each one keeps the same solution.

optional.stem: (Lesson 8.4) A clue says the suspect carried at least 12 stolen gems. Which inequality shows the number g of gems?
optional.explanation: 'At least 12' includes 12 and any number above it, so g ≥ 12.
choiceFeedback: 'At least' includes 12 itself, so the symbol must allow equal to as well as greater than.
This allows fewer than 12 gems. 'At least 12' makes 12 the smallest possible number, not the largest.
This rules out 12 itself along with everything above it. 'At least' points the other way and includes the boundary.
optional.stemEs: Una pista dice que el sospechoso llevaba al menos 12 gemas robadas. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra el número g de gemas?
optional.explanationEs: 'Al menos 12' incluye el 12 y cualquier número mayor, así que g ≥ 12.
hints: An inequality has two things to decide: which direction it points, and whether the boundary number is included.
'At least 12' means 12 itself is allowed, so the symbol needs an 'or equal to' part.
Start with the boundary: 12 counts. Now decide whether the gem count goes above 12 or below it, and pick the matching symbol.
hintsEs: Una desigualdad tiene dos cosas que decidir: hacia dónde apunta y si el número del límite se incluye.
'Al menos 12' significa que el 12 sí se permite, así que el símbolo necesita la parte 'o igual a'.
Empieza con el límite: el 12 cuenta. Ahora decide si el número de gemas sube por encima de 12 o baja, y elige el símbolo que corresponde.

optional.stem: (Lesson 8.5) Clue: the witness ran more than 15 feet, so d > 15. On the number line, what do you draw?
optional.explanation: 'Greater than' (>) is a strict symbol, so 15 is NOT included — open circle. Larger values work, so shade right.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'Greater than' (>) is a strict symbol, so 15 is NOT included — open circle.
Shading left would mean distances under 15 feet count, but the witness ran farther than that. Test d = 10 in d > 15 to check.
This includes 15 and shades the shorter distances. Ask whether running exactly 15 feet fits "more than 15," then check the direction with a sample value.
optional.stemEs: Pista: el testigo corrió más de 15 pies, así que d > 15. En la recta numérica, ¿qué dibujas?
optional.explanationEs: "Mayor que" (>) es un símbolo estricto, así que 15 NO está incluido: círculo abierto. Los valores mayores sí funcionan, así que se sombrea hacia la derecha.
hints: The circle shows whether the boundary number itself counts as a solution, and the shading shows every other number that works.
Decide first whether running exactly 15 feet fits the phrase "more than 15 feet."
Try d = 20 in d > 15 and see whether it works, then try d = 10. The side that passes the test is the side you shade.
hintsEs: El círculo muestra si el número límite cuenta como solución, y el sombreado muestra todos los demás números que funcionan.
Primero decide si correr exactamente 15 pies cumple con la frase "más de 15 pies".
Prueba d = 20 en d > 15 y observa si funciona; después prueba d = 10. El lado que pasa la prueba es el lado que se sombrea.
choicesEs: Círculo abierto en 15, sombrea a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 15, sombrea a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 15, sombrea a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 15, sombrea a la izquierda

optional.stem: (Lesson 8.6) Clue 1: Which value is a solution of x > 7?
optional.explanation: A solution makes x > 7 true. Substitute each: 9 > 7 is true, but 7 > 7, 5 > 7, and 3 > 7 are all false. So 9 is the solution that opens the gate.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. A solution makes x > 7 true.
Substituting gives 5 > 7, which is false. Look for a value that lands on the greater side of 7.
3 > 7 is not a true statement, so 3 cannot be in the solution set. Test each value by putting it into the inequality.
optional.stemEs: Pista 1: ¿cuál valor es una solución de x > 7?
optional.explanationEs: Una solución hace verdadera la desigualdad x > 7. Sustituye cada uno: 9 > 7 es verdadero, pero 7 > 7, 5 > 7 y 3 > 7 son todos falsos. Por eso 9 es la solución que abre la puerta.
hints: A solution is any value that makes the inequality a true statement.
Substitute each choice for x and decide whether the statement it creates is true.
Start at the bottom of the list: replace x with 3 and check whether 3 > 7 is true. Work up through the choices the same way.
hintsEs: Una solución es cualquier valor que hace verdadero el enunciado de la desigualdad.
Sustituye cada opción en lugar de x y decide si el enunciado que se forma es verdadero.
Empieza por el final de la lista: reemplaza x por 3 y comprueba si 3 > 7 es verdadero. Sigue subiendo por las opciones de la misma manera.

optional.stem: (Lesson 8.7) Room 2: The vault keypad clue reads, 'A number of stolen coins plus 6 equals 14.' Solve x + 6 = 14 to find the code x.
optional.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = ___.
6 is a number already given in the equation, not the unknown. Undo the +6 to find what x has to be.
Check this one by substituting it back: your value plus 6 has to land exactly on 14.
optional.stemEs: Sala 2: la pista del teclado de la bóveda dice: 'Un número de monedas robadas más 6 es igual a 14'. Resuelve x + 6 = 14 para hallar el código x.
optional.explanationEs: Resta 6 en los dos lados: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
hints: An equation is a balance — whatever you do to one side, you do to the other.
The 6 is being added to x, so undo it with the opposite operation, subtraction.
Subtract 6 from both sides so that x stands alone, then work out 14 − 6.
hintsEs: Una ecuación es un equilibrio: lo que le haces a un lado, se lo haces al otro.
Al x se le está sumando 6, así que deshazlo con la operación contraria, la resta.
Resta 6 en los dos lados para que la x quede sola y luego calcula 14 − 6.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 8.4) Which inequality represents: 'The temperature is less than 40 degrees'?
approaching.explanation: 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
The ≤ symbol lets the temperature be exactly 40. 'Less than 40' leaves 40 out.
An equals sign pins the temperature to a single value, but this situation describes a whole range of temperatures.
hints: Find the comparison phrase: 'less than 40 degrees'. Does 40 itself count, or only temperatures below it?
'Less than' with no 'or equal to' means a strict symbol — no bar underneath — pointing toward the smaller side.
Test a value: is 35 degrees 'less than 40'? Yes — so pick the strict symbol that puts t on the smaller side of 40.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'La temperatura es menor que 40 grados'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Menor que' significa <, así que la desigualdad es t < 40.
hintsEs: Halla la frase de comparación: 'menos de 40 grados'. ¿Cuenta el 40 mismo o solo las temperaturas por debajo?
'Menos que' sin 'o igual a' significa un símbolo estricto —sin barra debajo— apuntando hacia el lado menor.
Prueba un valor: ¿35 grados es 'menos de 40'? Sí, así que elige el símbolo estricto que pone t del lado menor de 40.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 8.4) Which inequality represents: 'You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride'?
approaching.explanation: 'At least' means greater than or equal to, so h ≥ 48.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'At least' means greater than or equal to, so h ≥ 48.
This describes riders who are too short to ride. Check which direction the symbol opens.
This would let anyone shorter than 48 inches ride. 'At least 48' makes 48 the smallest allowed height, not the largest.
hints: 'At least 48' — ask yourself: can a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall ride? That decides whether 48 is included.
When the boundary value is allowed, you need a symbol with the 'or equal to' bar under it.
Allowed heights are 48, 49, 50, and up. Pick the symbol that includes 48 itself AND points toward bigger numbers.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Debes medir al menos 48 pulgadas de estatura para subir'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Al menos' significa mayor que o igual a, así que h ≥ 48.
hintsEs: 'Al menos 48': pregúntate si alguien que mide EXACTAMENTE 48 pulgadas puede subir. Eso decide si el 48 se incluye.
Cuando el valor del límite sí se permite, necesitas un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual a' debajo.
Las estaturas permitidas son 48, 49, 50 y más. Elige el símbolo que incluya el 48 Y apunte hacia los números mayores.

approaching.explanation: x < 5 means 5 is NOT included (open circle) and values less than 5 are shaded (left).
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but < does not include 5, so the circle stays open.
This shades the values above 5. Test a number like 7 in x < 5 and see whether it belongs in the solution set.
This both fills in 5 and shades the larger side. Try x = 5 and x = 7 in the inequality — check whether either one makes it true.
hints: Every inequality graph asks two questions: is 5 itself a solution (circle type), and which side holds the solutions (shading)?
Strict symbols like < exclude the boundary, so check whether 5 makes x < 5 true. Then shade toward test values that work.
First step: 5 < 5 is false, so 5 is NOT included — that fixes the circle type. Now test x = 4 to find the shading direction.
approaching.explanationEs: x < 5 significa que 5 NO está incluido (círculo abierto) y se sombrean los valores menores que 5 (hacia la izquierda).
choicesEs: Círculo abierto en 5, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 5, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 5, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 5, sombreado a la derecha
hintsEs: Toda gráfica de desigualdad hace dos preguntas: ¿es 5 mismo una solución (tipo de círculo) y de qué lado están las soluciones (sombreado)?
Los símbolos estrictos como < excluyen el límite, así que revisa si 5 hace verdadera x < 5. Luego sombrea hacia los valores de prueba que sí funcionan.
Primer paso: 5 < 5 es falso, así que 5 NO se incluye; eso fija el tipo de círculo. Ahora prueba x = 4 para hallar la dirección del sombreado.

approaching.explanation: x ≥ 3 means 3 IS included (closed circle) and values greater than or equal to 3 are shaded (right).
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but ≥ includes 3, so the circle should be filled in.
This shades the numbers below 3. Test x = 1 in x ≥ 3 to see whether small values satisfy the inequality.
This leaves 3 out and shades the smaller side. Check whether x = 3 makes x ≥ 3 true, and test x = 1 as well.
hints: Check the symbol: ≥ has the 'or equal' bar. What does that bar mean for the circle at 3?
The bar means 3 IS a solution, so the circle gets filled in. Then a quick test value tells you the shading side.
First step: 3 ≥ 3 is true, so 3 is included. Now test x = 10 — is 10 ≥ 3 true? Shade toward that side.
approaching.explanationEs: x ≥ 3 significa que 3 SÍ está incluido (círculo cerrado) y se sombrean los valores mayores o iguales que 3 (hacia la derecha).
choicesEs: Círculo cerrado en 3, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 3, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 3, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 3, sombreado a la izquierda
hintsEs: Revisa el símbolo: ≥ tiene la barra de 'o igual'. ¿Qué significa esa barra para el círculo en el 3?
La barra significa que 3 SÍ es solución, así que el círculo se rellena. Luego un valor de prueba te dice el lado del sombreado.
Primer paso: 3 ≥ 3 es verdadero, así que el 3 se incluye. Ahora prueba x = 10: ¿es 10 ≥ 3 verdadero? Sombrea hacia ese lado.

approaching.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: x > 14 − 6 = 8. Graph: open circle at 8, shade right.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 6 from both sides: x > 14 − 6 = ___.
The boundary number is right, but the inequality symbol flipped. Adding or subtracting on both sides never changes the direction of the symbol.
An inequality has many solutions, not just one. Look at what the > symbol allows on either side of the boundary.
hints: Solve it like an equation: x has 6 added to it. The > symbol just rides along.
Subtract 6 from both sides — the inequality symbol keeps pointing the same way when you subtract.
Compute 14 − 6 and keep the >. Then test: pick a number bigger than your result and check it makes x + 6 > 14 true.
approaching.explanationEs: Resta 6 en ambos lados: x > 14 − 6 = 8. Gráfica: círculo abierto en 8, sombrea hacia la derecha.
hintsEs: Resuélvelo como una ecuación: a x se le suman 6. El símbolo > solo va de acompañante.
Resta 6 de ambos lados: el símbolo de desigualdad sigue apuntando igual cuando restas.
Calcula 14 − 6 y conserva el >. Luego prueba: escoge un número mayor que tu resultado y revisa que haga verdadera x + 6 > 14.

approaching.explanation: Add 9 to both sides: x ≤ 3 + 9 = 12. Graph: closed circle at 12, shade left.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 9 to both sides: x ≤ 3 + 9 = ___.
You found the right boundary, but the symbol turned around. Adding the same number to both sides keeps the original direction.
This names only the boundary value. The ≤ symbol includes that value and a whole range on one side of it.
hints: x has 9 subtracted from it. Undo that first; the ≤ symbol keeps its direction.
Add 9 to both sides. Adding the same number to both sides never flips the symbol.
Compute 3 + 9 and keep the ≤. Check by testing a value at or below your boundary in the original inequality.
approaching.explanationEs: Suma 9 en ambos lados: x ≤ 3 + 9 = 12. Gráfica: círculo cerrado en 12, sombrea hacia la izquierda.
hintsEs: A x se le restan 9. Deshaz eso primero; el símbolo ≤ conserva su dirección.
Suma 9 a ambos lados. Sumar el mismo número a ambos lados nunca voltea el símbolo.
Calcula 3 + 9 y conserva el ≤. Comprueba probando un valor igual o menor que tu límite en la desigualdad original.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 8.7) A museum has some paintings. After adding 12, they have 45. Which equation models this?
approaching.explanation: 'Adding 12' to the original number gives 45: p + 12 = 45. Solve: p = 33.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Solve: p = ___.
12p means 12 groups of p, which is multiplication. Re-read what actually happened to the paintings the museum already had.
Dividing would split the paintings into 12 equal groups. The museum did something different with the 12.
hints: The museum STARTS with an unknown number of paintings p, then 12 more are ADDED to reach 45.
'Adding 12' means the model joins p and 12 with a plus sign, and the total 45 goes after the equals sign.
Write the story in order: p, plus 12, equals 45. Which choice matches without switching the operation?
approaching.stemEs: Un museo tiene algunas pinturas. Después de agregar 12, tiene 45. ¿Qué ecuación representa esta situación?
approaching.explanationEs: «Agregar 12» al número original da 45: p + 12 = 45. Resuelve: p = 33.
hintsEs: El museo EMPIEZA con un número desconocido de cuadros p y luego se AGREGAN 12 más para llegar a 45.
'Agregar 12' significa que el modelo une p y 12 con un signo más, y el total 45 va después del signo igual.
Escribe la historia en orden: p, más 12, es igual a 45. ¿Qué opción coincide sin cambiar la operación?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 8.7) A detective needs more than 8 hours to finish the investigation. She has already worked 3 hours. Which inequality represents the additional hours h she needs?
approaching.explanation: 3 hours plus additional hours h must be more than 8: 3 + h > 8. Solve: h > 5.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Solve: h > 5.
This compares the extra hours to 3, but 3 is the time already worked, not the goal. It is the total of both amounts that has to pass 8.
The 8 and the 3 have swapped jobs here. 8 is the total she must go past, and 3 is what she has already finished.
hints: There are two time pieces: the 3 hours already worked and the extra hours h. Together they must pass 8 hours.
'More than 8' means the TOTAL of 3 + h sits on the big side of a strict inequality — not an equals sign.
Combine first: 3 + h. Then compare that total to 8 using the strict 'more than' symbol. Which choice is built that way?
approaching.stemEs: Una detective necesita más de 8 horas para terminar la investigación. Ya trabajó 3 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa las horas adicionales h que necesita?
approaching.explanationEs: 3 horas más las horas adicionales h deben ser más de 8: 3 + h > 8. Resuelve: h > 5.
hintsEs: Hay dos partes de tiempo: las 3 horas ya trabajadas y las horas extra h. Juntas deben pasar de 8 horas.
'Más de 8' significa que el TOTAL de 3 + h queda del lado grande de una desigualdad estricta, no de un signo igual.
Combina primero: 3 + h. Luego compara ese total con 8 usando el símbolo estricto de 'más de'. ¿Qué opción está armada así?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 8.4) A parking garage charges if your stay is more than 2 hours. Which inequality represents times t that are charged?
onLevel.explanation: 'More than 2 hours' means strictly greater than: t > 2. Exactly 2 hours is not charged.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'More than 2 hours' means strictly greater than: t > 2.
This describes short stays, which are not charged. Check which side of 2 the symbol opens toward.
This would charge a stay of exactly 2 hours, and it also covers shorter stays. 'More than 2' leaves 2 out and looks above it.
hints: The charge starts once the stay goes PAST 2 hours. Is a stay of exactly 2 hours charged?
If exactly 2 hours is NOT charged, the boundary is excluded — that rules out any symbol with the 'or equal' bar.
Test t = 2 and t = 3: only stays longer than 2 are charged. Pick the symbol that makes t = 3 true but t = 2 false.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estacionamiento cobra si tu estancia dura más de 2 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa los tiempos t que se cobran?
onLevel.explanationEs: 'Más de 2 horas' significa estrictamente mayor que: t > 2. Exactamente 2 horas no se cobra.
hintsEs: El cobro empieza cuando la estancia PASA de 2 horas. ¿Se cobra una estancia de exactamente 2 horas?
Si exactamente 2 horas NO se cobra, el límite queda excluido: eso descarta cualquier símbolo con la barra de 'o igual'.
Prueba t = 2 y t = 3: solo se cobran las estancias mayores de 2. Elige el símbolo que haga verdadero t = 3 y falso t = 2.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 8.4) Crack the Inequality Error

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: The report says no fewer than 9 witnesses saw the suspect.
workedExample.workEs: El informe dice que no menos de 9 testigos vieron al sospechoso.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let w stand for the number of witnesses.
workedExample.workEs: Sea w el número de testigos.

onLevel.correctWork: 'No fewer than 9' means the count cannot drop below 9 — 9 or more witnesses is required. That is w ≥ 9, not w < 9, which would only allow numbers below 9, the opposite of what the clue says.
hints: Does 'no fewer than 9' rule out having 9 witnesses, or does it rule out having fewer than 9?
'No fewer than' means 'at least,' so use ≥. The correct inequality is w ≥ 9.
onLevel.titleEs: Resuelve el error de la desigualdad
onLevel.explanation: The inequality step pointed the symbol the wrong way. "No fewer than 9" means the count can never drop below 9, so 9 and every larger number works: w ≥ 9. The w < 9 that was written allows only counts under 9, which is the opposite of the clue.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la desigualdad apuntó el símbolo en la dirección equivocada. "No menos de 9" significa que el conteo nunca puede bajar de 9, así que sirven 9 y todos los números mayores: w ≥ 9. El w < 9 que se escribió solo permite conteos menores que 9, justo lo contrario de la pista.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 'No menos de 9' significa que el conteo no puede bajar de 9 — se requieren 9 testigos o más. Eso es w ≥ 9, no w < 9, que solo permitiría números por debajo de 9, lo contrario de lo que dice la pista.
hintsEs: ¿'No menos de 9' descarta tener 9 testigos, o descarta tener menos de 9?
'No menos de' significa 'al menos', así que usa ≥. La desigualdad correcta es w ≥ 9.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 8.5) A number line shows a closed circle at 8 and is shaded to the left. Which inequality does this represent?
onLevel.explanation: Closed circle means the value is included (≤ or ≥). Shaded left means less than or equal to: x ≤ 8.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Closed circle means the value is included (≤ or ≥).
This symbol points the solutions toward the larger numbers, but the graph is shaded toward the smaller ones. Match the shading direction to the symbol before choosing.
This symbol leaves 8 out and points toward larger values, while the graph shows a filled circle and shading to the left. Line up both features.
hints: Read the graph's two clues: the circle at 8 is CLOSED, and the shading runs LEFT toward smaller numbers.
A closed circle means 8 itself is a solution, so the symbol needs the 'or equal' bar. Shading left means solutions are 8 or smaller.
Test x = 5 (in the shaded part) and x = 8 (the circle): both must make the inequality true. Which choice passes both tests?
onLevel.stemEs: Una recta numérica muestra un círculo cerrado en 8 y está sombreada hacia la izquierda. ¿Qué desigualdad representa esto?
onLevel.explanationEs: El círculo cerrado significa que el valor está incluido (≤ o ≥). El sombreado hacia la izquierda significa menor o igual que: x ≤ 8.
hintsEs: Lee las dos pistas de la gráfica: el círculo en el 8 está CERRADO y el sombreado va a la IZQUIERDA, hacia los números menores.
Un círculo cerrado significa que el 8 sí es solución, así que el símbolo necesita la barra de 'o igual'. Sombrear a la izquierda significa que las soluciones son 8 o menos.
Prueba x = 5 (en la parte sombreada) y x = 8 (el círculo): ambos deben hacer verdadera la desigualdad. ¿Qué opción pasa las dos pruebas?

onLevel.title: (Lesson 8.5) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: The case file needs fewer than 9 clues, so c < 9. Graph it.
workedExample.workEs: El expediente necesita menos de 9 pistas, así que c < 9. Grafícalo.

workedExample.label: Final graph
workedExample.workEs: Círculo abierto en 9, sombreado a la derecha

onLevel.correctWork: The circle choice was correct — c < 9 does not include 9, so it needs an open circle. But 'less than' means smaller values, so the shading should go LEFT toward smaller numbers, not right. Final graph: open circle at 9, shaded left.
hints: The circle type and the shading direction are two separate decisions — check both.
< and ≤ shade LEFT toward smaller values. > and ≥ shade RIGHT toward larger values.
onLevel.explanation: The open circle at 9 is correct because c < 9 leaves 9 out, but the shade direction step goes the wrong way. 'Fewer than 9 clues' means values smaller than 9, so the shading runs left, giving an open circle at 9 shaded left.
onLevel.explanationEs: El círculo abierto en 9 está correcto porque c < 9 deja fuera al 9, pero el paso de la dirección del sombreado va al lado equivocado. «Menos de 9 pistas» significa valores menores que 9, así que el sombreado va hacia la izquierda: círculo abierto en 9 sombreado a la izquierda.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La elección del círculo era correcta — c < 9 no incluye el 9, así que necesita un círculo abierto. Pero 'menos que' significa valores más pequeños, así que el sombreado debe ir a la IZQUIERDA hacia los números menores, no a la derecha. Gráfica final: círculo abierto en 9, sombreado a la izquierda.
hintsEs: El tipo de círculo y la dirección del sombreado son dos decisiones distintas — revisa las dos.
< y ≤ sombrean a la IZQUIERDA hacia los valores menores. > y ≥ sombrean a la DERECHA hacia los valores mayores.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 8.6) Is x = 5 a solution to x + 4 > 12?
choices: No, because 5 + 4 = 9, and 9 is not greater than 12
onLevel.explanation: Substitute: 5 + 4 = 9. Since 9 > 12 is false, x = 5 is NOT a solution.
choiceFeedback: Your arithmetic is right, but then compare: is 9 actually greater than 12?
Comparing 5 with the 4 in the expression skips the actual test. Substitute 5 for x, simplify the left side, then compare that result with 12.
Comparing x directly with 12 leaves out the + 4. Substitute first, then compare the simplified left side with 12.
hints: 'Is 5 a solution?' means: substitute 5 for x and see whether the statement comes out TRUE.
Replace x with 5 and compute the left side completely. Then compare that result to 12 honestly — is it really greater?
Compute 5 + 4 first. Then ask: is that total greater than 12? Your yes-or-no needs the correct REASON attached to it.
onLevel.explanationEs: Sustituye: 5 + 4 = 9. Como 9 > 12 es falso, x = 5 NO es una solución.
choicesEs: No, porque 5 + 4 = 9, y 9 no es mayor que 12
hintsEs: '¿Es 5 una solución?' significa: sustituye 5 por x y ve si el enunciado resulta VERDADERO.
Reemplaza x por 5 y calcula el lado izquierdo completo. Luego compara ese resultado con 12 con honestidad: ¿de verdad es mayor?
Calcula primero 5 + 4. Luego pregunta: ¿ese total es mayor que 12? Tu sí o no necesita llevar la RAZÓN correcta.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 8.6) Catch the Open vs. Closed Circle Mistake

workedExample.label: Graph
workedExample.workEs: Círculo abierto en 13, sombrea a la derecha

onLevel.correctWork: The solving is correct: x ≥ 13. But the symbol ≥ means 'greater than OR equal to,' so 13 IS a solution and must be included. Use a CLOSED circle at 13 (not open), then shade right.
hints: Does the symbol ≥ include the boundary value 13, or leave it out?
≥ and ≤ use a closed circle; only < and > use an open circle. Here use a closed circle at 13.
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error del círculo abierto o cerrado
onLevel.explanation: The solving is correct — adding 4 to both sides gives x ≥ 13 — but the graph left the boundary out. The symbol ≥ means "greater than or equal to," so 13 is itself a solution and must be filled in: a closed circle at 13, shaded to the right.
onLevel.explanationEs: La parte de resolver está bien: sumar 4 en ambos lados da x ≥ 13, pero la gráfica dejó fuera el valor límite. El símbolo ≥ significa "mayor que o igual a", así que 13 sí es solución y debe marcarse relleno: círculo cerrado en 13, sombreado hacia la derecha.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La resolución es correcta: x ≥ 13. Pero el símbolo ≥ significa 'mayor O igual que', así que 13 SÍ es solución y debe incluirse. Usa un círculo CERRADO en 13 (no abierto), y luego sombrea a la derecha.
hintsEs: ¿El símbolo ≥ incluye el valor límite 13, o lo deja fuera?
≥ y ≤ usan un círculo cerrado; solo < y > usan un círculo abierto. Aquí usa un círculo cerrado en 13.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 8.7) A student solved 4n = 52 and got n = 13. Is the answer reasonable if n represents the number of notebooks in a box?
choices: Yes — 13 notebooks per box is reasonable
Yes — but only if n is a fraction
onLevel.explanation: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.
48 comes from subtracting 4 from 52, but 4n means 4 times n. Multiplication is undone with division.
Notebooks are counted in whole numbers, and substituting the solution back into 4n = 52 works out exactly. No fraction is needed here.
hints: 'Reasonable' asks two things: does the math check out, AND does the number make sense for notebooks in a box?
Check the math first: multiply 4 by 13 and see if it rebuilds 52. Then judge whether that count fits a real box of notebooks.
Compute 4 × 13. Does it equal 52? Then ask: could a box realistically hold that many notebooks? Match your reasoning to one choice.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estudiante resolvió 4n = 52 y obtuvo n = 13. ¿Es razonable la respuesta si n representa el número de cuadernos en una caja?
onLevel.explanationEs: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 cuadernos por caja es una respuesta razonable con un número entero.
choicesEs: Sí — 13 cuadernos por caja es razonable
Sí — pero solo si n es una fracción
hintsEs: 'Razonable' pregunta dos cosas: ¿cuadran las cuentas Y tiene sentido ese número de cuadernos en una caja?
Revisa primero las cuentas: multiplica 4 por 13 y ve si reconstruye 52. Luego juzga si esa cantidad cabe en una caja real de cuadernos.
Calcula 4 × 13. ¿Da 52? Luego pregunta: ¿podría una caja tener realmente esa cantidad de cuadernos? Une tu razonamiento con una opción.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 8.7) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Seven evidence lockers hold 84 case files in all, split equally. How many files per locker?
workedExample.workEs: Siete casilleros de evidencia guardan 84 expedientes en total, repartidos por igual. ¿Cuántos expedientes por casillero?

onLevel.correctWork: The variable f is multiplied by 7, so you undo it by dividing both sides by 7 (the inverse operation), not by subtracting 7. 7f = 84 becomes f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12. So there are 12 files per locker. Check: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
hints: f is multiplied by 7. What operation undoes multiplying by 7 — subtracting 7 or dividing by 7?
Divide both sides by 7: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 files per locker.
onLevel.explanation: The model 7f = 84 is correct, but f is MULTIPLIED by 7, and subtracting 7 does not undo a multiplication. Divide both sides by 7 instead: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 files per locker. Check: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
onLevel.explanationEs: El modelo 7f = 84 está correcto, pero la f está MULTIPLICADA por 7, y restar 7 no deshace una multiplicación. Hay que dividir ambos lados entre 7: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 archivos por casillero. Comprueba: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La variable f está multiplicada por 7, así que se deshace dividiendo ambos lados entre 7 (la operación inversa), no restando 7. 7f = 84 se convierte en f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12. Así que hay 12 expedientes por casillero. Comprueba: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
hintsEs: f está multiplicada por 7. ¿Qué operación deshace multiplicar por 7 — restar 7 o dividir entre 7?
Divide ambos lados entre 7: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 archivos por casillero.

extending.title: (Lesson 8.4) Find the Inequality Error

workedExample.label: Situation
workedExample.work: No more than 25 students can join the field trip
workedExample.workEs: No más de 25 estudiantes pueden ir a la excursión

extending.correctWork: 'No more than' means less than or equal to (≤), not greater than. The correct inequality is s ≤ 25.
hints: 'No more than 25' means the number cannot exceed 25. Is that greater than or less than or equal to?
'No more than' = at most = ≤. The correct inequality is s ≤ 25.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la desigualdad
extending.explanation: The key-phrase step read "no more than" as greater than, but that phrase puts a cap on the group — the number of students can never go above 25. It means "at most," so the model is s ≤ 25, which allows 25 and every smaller count.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de la frase clave interpretó "no más de" como mayor que, pero esa frase pone un tope al grupo: el número de estudiantes nunca puede pasar de 25. Significa "a lo más", así que el modelo es s ≤ 25, que permite 25 y todos los conteos menores.
extending.correctWorkEs: 'No más de' significa menor o igual que (≤), no mayor que. La desigualdad correcta es s ≤ 25.
hintsEs: 'No más de 25' significa que el número no puede pasar de 25. ¿Eso es mayor que o menor o igual que?
'No más de' = como máximo = ≤. La desigualdad correcta es s ≤ 25.

extending.title: (Lesson 8.5) Find the Graphing Error

workedExample.label: Graph
workedExample.workEs: Círculo cerrado en 6, sombreado a la derecha

extending.correctWork: x > 6 uses a strict inequality (no 'equal to'), so the circle should be OPEN, not closed. Open circle at 6, shaded right.
hints: Look at the inequality symbol carefully. Is it > or ≥?
> means strictly greater than — 6 is NOT included, so the circle must be open.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la gráfica
extending.explanation: The shading right matches x > 6, but the circle type step used a closed circle. Since > is strict, 6 > 6 is false and 6 is not a solution, so the graph needs an open circle at 6 shaded right.
extending.explanationEs: El sombreado a la derecha coincide con x > 6, pero el paso del tipo de círculo usó un círculo cerrado. Como > es estricto, 6 > 6 es falso y el 6 no es solución, así que la gráfica necesita un círculo abierto en 6 sombreado a la derecha.
extending.correctWorkEs: x > 6 usa una desigualdad estricta (sin 'igual a'), así que el círculo debe ser ABIERTO, no cerrado. Círculo abierto en 6, sombreado a la derecha.
hintsEs: Mira con cuidado el símbolo de desigualdad. ¿Es > o ≥?
> significa estrictamente mayor que — el 6 NO se incluye, así que el círculo debe quedar abierto.

extending.title: (Lesson 8.6) Find the Solving Error

workedExample.label: Graph
workedExample.workEs: Círculo cerrado en 7, sombrea a la derecha

extending.correctWork: The inverse of subtracting 8 is ADDING 8, not subtracting. Add 8 to both sides: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23. Graph: closed circle at 23, shade right.
hints: The equation has − 8. What is the inverse of subtracting 8?
To undo − 8, you add 8 to both sides: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23.
extending.explanation: The inequality shows − 8, and the inverse of subtracting is adding. Adding 8 to both sides gives x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23, not 7. The graph is a closed circle at 23 shaded to the right, since ≥ includes the boundary value.
extending.explanationEs: La desigualdad muestra − 8, y lo inverso de restar es sumar. Al sumar 8 en ambos lados: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23, no 7. La gráfica lleva un círculo cerrado en 23 sombreado hacia la derecha, porque ≥ incluye el valor límite.
extending.correctWorkEs: La inversa de restar 8 es SUMAR 8, no restar. Suma 8 a ambos lados: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23. Gráfica: círculo cerrado en 23, sombrea a la derecha.
hintsEs: La ecuación tiene − 8. ¿Cuál es la operación inversa de restar 8?
Para deshacer − 8, sumas 8 a ambos lados: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23.

extending.title: (Lesson 8.7) Find the Problem-Solving Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A parking lot holds at most 200 cars. There are 134 already. How many more can park?
workedExample.workEs: Un estacionamiento admite como máximo 200 autos. Ya hay 134. ¿Cuántos más pueden estacionarse?

extending.correctWork: 'At most' means less than or equal to, so the model should be an inequality: 134 + c ≤ 200. Solving: c ≤ 66. Up to 66 more cars can park, not exactly 66.
hints: The problem says 'at most 200.' Does that mean exactly 200 or up to 200?
'At most' requires ≤, not =. The correct model is 134 + c ≤ 200, so c ≤ 66.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error al resolver el problema
extending.explanation: The arithmetic is fine, but the model is too strict. 'At most 200 cars' means the lot can hold 200 or fewer, which is ≤, not =. The model should be 134 + c ≤ 200, giving c ≤ 66 — up to 66 more cars can park, not exactly 66.
extending.explanationEs: Las cuentas están bien, pero el modelo es demasiado estricto. 'At most 200 cars' significa que el estacionamiento puede tener 200 o menos, y eso es ≤, no =. El modelo debe ser 134 + c ≤ 200, lo que da c ≤ 66: pueden estacionarse hasta 66 autos más, no exactamente 66.
extending.correctWorkEs: 'Como máximo' significa menor o igual que, así que el modelo debe ser una desigualdad: 134 + c ≤ 200. Al resolver: c ≤ 66. Hasta 66 autos más pueden estacionarse, no exactamente 66.
hintsEs: El problema dice 'como máximo 200'. ¿Eso significa exactamente 200 o hasta 200?
'Como máximo' requiere ≤, no =. El modelo correcto es 134 + c ≤ 200, así que c ≤ 66.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving is matching the wrong model to a key phrase. For 'the getaway car held no more than 6 bags,' students often write the equation b = 6 instead of the inequality b ≤ 6, because they see one number and assume it must be exact. The same mistake happens in reverse: for 'the reward split equally among 5 people gave each $40,' students sometimes write the inequality 5p ≥ 40 instead of the equation 5p = 40, because 'split equally' sounds like it could mean a range. Before you submit, ask: does this phrase give one exact value (equation, =) or a limit/range (inequality, <, >, ≤, ≥)?

diagram.title: Detective's Budget Limit
diagram.caption: She has spent $320 of her $500 cap (closed dot = allowed), so the gap up to $500 shows r ≤ 180 — at most $180 more.

connect.scenario: A detective has a $500 budget for equipment. She has already spent $320. The inequality 320 + r ≤ 500 represents the remaining amount r she can spend. She also needs exactly 4 flashlights at $15 each, represented by the equation 4f = 60.
connect.promptQuestion: How much more can the detective spend? How much does each flashlight cost? When do you use an equation versus an inequality?
connect.prompt: The detective can spend at most $__ more because r ≤ 500 − ___ = ___. Each flashlight costs $__ because f = 60 ÷ ___ = ___.

check.explanation: Subtract 320 from both sides: r ≤ 500 − 320 = 180. She can spend at most $180 more.
Divide both sides by 4: f = 60 ÷ 4 = $15 per flashlight.

check.stem: Why is one an equation and the other an inequality?
choices: The flashlights cost exactly $60, but the budget is a limit she must stay under
Because equations are for money and inequalities are for counting
check.explanation: 'Exactly' points to one value, so it is an equation. A budget — 'at most' — allows a whole range of values, so it is an inequality.

connect.modelAnswer: Budget: 320 + r ≤ 500, so r ≤ 180 — she can spend at most $180 more. Flashlights: 4f = 60, so f = $15 each. The budget is an inequality because any amount up to $180 is allowed; the flashlight cost is an equation because there is exactly one answer.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 8.5) How would you graph the inequality x ≥ 9?
exitTicket.explanation: x ≥ 9 means 9 is included (closed circle) and values are 9 or greater (shaded right).
choiceFeedback: '≥' includes 9, so the circle should be filled/closed.
x ≥ 9 means 9 and up — shade toward larger numbers.
Both parts are off — '≥' is a closed circle, shaded right.
hints: Break the graph into two decisions: is 9 itself a solution, and which direction do the solutions go?
The 'or equal' bar means the boundary counts — that sets your circle type. Then test a bigger number to find the shading.
First check 9 ≥ 9 — true or false? That decides the circle. Then test x = 12 to see which side of 9 gets shaded.

questions.explanation: Add 4 to both sides: x < 11 + 4 = 15. Graph: open circle at 15, shade left.
Subtract 6 from both sides: x > 14 − 6 = 8. Graph: open circle at 8, shade right.
Subtract 10 from both sides: x ≥ 25 − 10 = 15. Graph: closed circle at 15, shade right.
Add 9 to both sides: x ≤ 3 + 9 = 12. Graph: closed circle at 12, shade left.

Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.

Empieza así: El valor de frontera es 5.
